description:
A ceasefire has come into effect in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky, on the front line of the war with Russia. Thousands of residents have been trapped there, cut off from food, water and electricity.

The ceasefire has been brokered by an unexpected figure: the US First Lady Melania Trump. But the Vatican is also claiming credit for the truce, raising questions about who helped bring it about – and what it might mean for the people caught up in the fighting.

After years of war and worsening conditions for civilians, a pause in the fighting could offer some relief. But how much protection will it really provide? And can this ceasefire hold?

The Global Story’s Tristan Redman speaks to Simon Shuster of The Atlantic about the state of the war, the future of US support and why Kyiv is increasingly worried about being left out of the room.

author: BBC News
description:
With counting almost complete in Israel's first general election since the 7th October attacks by Hamas and the start of the war in Gaza, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is in the lead. But neither Mr Netanyahu, nor his main opponent, Gadi Eisenkot, have enough support to form a government. They will now have to seek out fresh political alliances, or coax opposition members onto their side. 

We'll take a look at how that could play out, and where this election leaves the Palestinian people. Would a coalition led by Mr Eisenkot take a different tack on Gaza, the occupied West Bank or Palestinian statehood? 

00:00 Introduction 
01:30 How do Israelis feel about the election deadlock? 
03:20 What will it take for Netanyahu or Eisenkot to form a government?
06:08 What does the Israeli election mean for Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank?

description:
At least 64 people have been killed after a Spanish high-speed train collided with another south of the capital Madrid, officials say.
 
The updated death toll makes the rail disaster the country's worst since 2013, when 80 people died after a train derailed in north-western Spain.
 
Investigations are ongoing but Francisco Badea, a professor of engineering at Nebrija University, says unacceptable failures in the system likely occurred before the deadly crash.
 
More than 500 passengers were travelling on the trains involved in Wednesday's collision, the spokesperson for the regional government says.

author: BBC News
description:
The death toll is continuing to rise after two trains collided south of Madrid in Spain. Watch live for updates on what we know so far.

More than 500 passengers were travelling on the trains involved, and the death toll "will almost certainly rise", according to the spokesperson for the regional government.

Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez says he is "shocked by the serious train accident" and is in constant contact with the transport minister.

Rail operator Adif says the incident occurred between a Renfe train and another of the Iryo company, which covers the Madrid to Seville route.

A spokesperson for the Spanish emergency services tells AFP "all resources are currently being deployed" including "several fire crews, three helicopters, and two mobile intensive care units".

description:
The US state department has told the BBC it will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family as Brazilian authorities question his whereabouts.
 
Police in Brazil say they cancelled the senator's passports after he failed to comply with a Supreme Court order to surrender the documents.
 
Reports from several media outlets suggest that the presidential candidate has travelled to the US.
 
"Those who have nothing to hide have nothing to fear," says newly re-elected Brazilian President Lula, remarking on his rival's whereabouts.
